```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Wiczling_2016_dexmedetomidine"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Wiczling_2016_dexmedetomidine"))$description`
* Article: [J Pharmacokinet Pharmacodyn 2016;43(3):315-324](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10928-016-9474-0) (open access)

Wiczling 2016 fitted a two-compartment model to dexmedetomidine
concentrations from critically ill children who received the drug as a
continuous infusion for two to ten days. The analysis was fully Bayesian
(WinBUGS), with informative priors on the typical values and the
between-subject variability taken from the pooled paediatric analysis of
Potts 2009 (Table 1). Clearances and volumes are scaled allometrically to a
70-kg adult, clearance matures with postmenstrual age, and every disposition
parameter is allowed to differ between the two sampling occasions (the first
24 h of the infusion and the 8 h after it stopped). The central volume was
1.5-fold larger on the second occasion and clearance 1.3-fold larger.

```{r model}
mod <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Wiczling_2016_dexmedetomidine"))
mod
```

# Population

Thirty-eight children (23 male, 15 female) were studied in the paediatric ICU
of Poznan University of Medical Sciences: median (range) age 70 (1.4-188.6)
months and weight 18.5 (4.7-60) kg (Table 2). Diagnoses were acute
respiratory failure (18), severe sepsis or septic shock (10), multiple or brain
trauma (8) and acute cardiac insufficiency (2); the median PRISM score was 0.5
(0-11). Dexmedetomidine was added to sufentanil + midazolam sedation, started
at 0.8 ug/kg/h and titrated in 0.2 ug/kg/h steps (maximum 1.4 ug/kg/h) to a
Cook score of 7-14, then stepped down to the minimum rate before stopping.
The median infusion lasted 97.3 h (45.0-229.2) and the median total dose was
1153.8 ug. Plasma was sampled at 1, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20 and 24 h after the start
(occasion 1) and just before and 5, 10, 20 min and 1, 2, 4 and 6 h after the
end of the infusion (occasion 2); 470 concentrations were analysed.

```{r population}
str(mod$population)
```

# Source trace

| Element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Two-compartment structure, infusion into central | -- | Methods equations 1-2; supplement Component Pascal ODE `DexTwoCptModelTCLRK45OCC` |
| `lcl` | log(41.6) L/h per 70 kg | Table 3, theta CL mean |
| `lq` | log(56.8) L/h per 70 kg | Table 3, theta Q mean |
| `lvc` | log(52.0) L per 70 kg | Table 3, theta V1 mean |
| `lvp` | log(70.4) L per 70 kg | Table 3, theta V2 mean |
| `ltm50_cl` | log(42.5) weeks | Table 3, theta TE50 mean |
| `lhill_cl` | log(2.45) | Table 3, theta Hill mean |
| `e_wt_cl`, `e_wt_q` | 0.75 (fixed) | Methods equation 5 |
| `e_wt_vc`, `e_wt_vp` | 1 (fixed) | Methods equation 5 |
| `e_occ2_cl` | 0.31 | Table 3, f CL = 1.31 |
| `e_occ2_q` | 0.02 | Table 3, f Q = 1.02 |
| `e_occ2_vc` | 0.50 | Table 3, f V1 = 1.50 |
| `e_occ2_vp` | -0.14 | Table 3, f V2 = 0.86 |
| Postmenstrual age = 4 x age (months) + 40 weeks | -- | supplement WinBUGS code, `logthetaMean[i, 1]` |
| Occasion switch `expit(t - 30)` | -- | supplement ODE component (`NNN` = 1, `TCL50` = 30) and WinBUGS `Vc[i]` |
| IIV covariance (CL, Q, V1, V2) | see model | Table 2S, Omega posterior means |
| `expSd` | 0.275 | Table 2S, sigma C |
| `nu` | 1.75 | Table 2S, nu |

The variances reproduce the coefficients of variation quoted in the Results
(56, 83, 152 and 68% for CL, Q, V1 and V2) and the Q-V1 correlation of 0.7:

```{r iiv-check}
om <- mod$omega
cv <- sqrt(exp(diag(om)) - 1) * 100
corr_qv1 <- om["etalq", "etalvc"] / sqrt(om["etalq", "etalq"] * om["etalvc", "etalvc"])
knitr::kable(
  data.frame(
    Parameter = c("CL", "Q", "V1", "V2"),
    `Model CV (%)` = round(cv, 0),
    `Paper CV (%)` = c(56, 83, 152, 68),
    check.names = FALSE
  ),
  row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "IIV as %CV from the Table 2S covariance matrix vs the Results text."
)
stopifnot(
  all(abs(round(cv) - c(56, 83, 152, 68)) <= 1),
  abs(corr_qv1 - 0.68) < 0.01
)
corr_qv1
```

# Typical clearance and volume by age (Figure 3)

Figure 3 plots each child's clearance and steady-state volume, both absolute
and per kg of body weight, against age. The per-kg volume is the same for
every child, 1.73 L/kg, because volumes scale linearly with weight and have no
age term: it equals (V1 + V2) / 70 kg. The per-kg clearance falls from about
0.85 L/h/kg in pre-school children to about 0.65 L/h/kg in adolescents (the
0.75 allometric exponent) and is lower again in the youngest infants
(maturation).

The virtual children below take the median weight for age from a reference
growth curve (CDC/WHO 50th percentile, sexes pooled); the points read from the
lower panels of Figure 3 are bin medians digitised by the maintainers.

```{r fig3}
growth <- data.frame(
  age_mo = c(0, 3, 6, 12, 24, 36, 60, 96, 120, 144, 168, 192),
  wt = c(3.4, 6.0, 7.6, 9.6, 12.2, 14.3, 18.4, 25.6, 32.0, 40.0, 50.0, 58.0)
)
typ <- data.frame(PNA = seq(1, 192, by = 1)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(WT = approx(growth$age_mo, growth$wt, PNA)$y)

ev_typ <- typ |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = dplyr::row_number(), time = 1, evid = 0, cmt = "central")
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), ev_typ, keep = c("PNA", "WT")) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(cl_per_kg = cl / WT, vss_per_kg = (vc + vp) / WT)

fig3_digitised <- data.frame(
  age_bin = c("< 6 months", "35-110 months", "140-195 months"),
  PNA = c(3, 70, 175),
  cl_per_kg_paper = c(0.69, 0.82, 0.64)
)

ggplot(sim_typ, aes(PNA, cl_per_kg)) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(data = fig3_digitised, aes(PNA, cl_per_kg_paper), shape = 1, size = 3) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(
    x = "Age (months)", y = "CL / BW (L/h/kg)",
    caption = paste(
      "Line: typical CL per kg at the median weight for age (occasion 1).",
      "Circles: bin medians read from Figure 3 (lower left) of Wiczling 2016."
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw()

fig3_cmp <- fig3_digitised |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(sim_typ, PNA, cl_per_kg), by = "PNA") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (cl_per_kg - cl_per_kg_paper) / cl_per_kg_paper)
fig3_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Age bin" = age_bin, "Age (months)" = PNA,
    "Figure 3 CL/BW (L/h/kg)" = cl_per_kg_paper,
    "Model CL/BW (L/h/kg)" = cl_per_kg, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Typical CL per kg vs Figure 3.")

vss_per_kg <- unique(signif(sim_typ$vss_per_kg, 6))
vss_per_kg
stopifnot(
  # Volumes are exactly proportional to weight, so Vss/BW is one number.
  length(vss_per_kg) == 1,
  abs(vss_per_kg / 1.73 - 1) < 0.03,
  # Digitised from a scatter of individual values, weights approximated by a
  # growth curve: a centre check, not a point-by-point one.
  all(abs(fig3_cmp$pct_diff) < 15)
)
```

# Occasion switch and steady state

For a typical 18.5-kg, 70-month-old child on the starting rate of 0.8 ug/kg/h,
the concentration at 24 h is within a few percent of the occasion-1 steady
state, rate / CL. After 30 h the occasion-2 parameters take over: the larger
central volume and clearance lower the concentration toward the new steady
state rate / (1.31 CL).

```{r typical}
wt <- 18.5
rate <- 0.8 * wt
ev_t <- rxode2::et(amt = rate * 97, rate = rate, cmt = "central") |>
  rxode2::et(sort(unique(c(seq(0, 96, by = 0.5), 97 + seq(0, 8, by = 1 / 12)))), cmt = "central") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(WT = wt, PNA = 70)
sim_t <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), ev_t) |> as.data.frame()

ggplot(sim_t, aes(time, Cc)) +
  geom_line(colour = "steelblue", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 30, linetype = 2) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after infusion start (h)", y = "Dexmedetomidine (ng/mL)",
    caption = "Typical child, 0.8 ug/kg/h for 97 h; dashed line = occasion switch at 30 h."
  ) +
  theme_bw()

# At 24 h the logistic switch is at expit(-6) = 0.25%, so the occasion-1
# clearance is taken at t = 0 for the ratio check.
cl_occ1 <- sim_t$cl[sim_t$time == 0]
css1 <- rate / sim_t$cl[sim_t$time == 24]
c24 <- sim_t$Cc[sim_t$time == 24]
c96 <- sim_t$Cc[sim_t$time == 96]
css2 <- rate / sim_t$cl[sim_t$time == 96]
c(c24 = c24, css_occ1 = css1, c96 = c96, css_occ2 = css2)
stopifnot(
  abs(c24 / css1 - 1) < 0.03,
  abs(c96 / css2 - 1) < 0.01,
  abs(sim_t$cl[sim_t$time == 96] / cl_occ1 - 1.31) < 1e-3
)
```

# Virtual cohort and posterior predictive check (Figure 2)

The study's infusions were individually titrated and the published material
does not give each child's rate history, so an exact replication of Figure 2
is not possible. As an illustration, 200 virtual children receive the starting
rate of 0.8 ug/kg/h for 97 h (the median infusion duration) and are sampled on
the study schedule. Age is drawn to match Table 2 (median about 70 months,
range 1.4-188.6) and weight from the growth curve above with 15% scatter.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20160601)
n_sub <- 200
cohort <- data.frame(id = seq_len(n_sub)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    PNA = 1.4 + 187.2 * rbeta(n_sub, 1.1, 1.9),
    WT = approx(growth$age_mo, growth$wt, PNA)$y * exp(rnorm(n_sub, 0, 0.15)),
    WT = pmin(pmax(WT, 4.7), 60)
  )
c(median_age = median(cohort$PNA), median_wt = median(cohort$WT))

t_end <- 97
obs_t <- c(1, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, t_end - 0.01, t_end + c(5, 10, 20) / 60, t_end + c(1, 2, 4, 6))
ev_c <- cohort |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::reframe(
    id = id,
    time = c(0, obs_t),
    evid = c(1, rep(0, length(obs_t))),
    amt = c(0.8 * WT * t_end, rep(0, length(obs_t))),
    rate = c(0.8 * WT, rep(0, length(obs_t))),
    cmt = "central",
    WT = WT, PNA = PNA
  )

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20160602)
sim_c <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_c, keep = c("WT", "PNA")) |>
  as.data.frame()

vpc <- sim_c |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    occasion = ifelse(time < 30, "Occasion 1: time after infusion start (h)",
                      "Occasion 2: time after infusion end (h)"),
    tplot = ifelse(time < 30, time, pmax(time - t_end, 0))
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(occasion, tplot) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p10 = quantile(sim, 0.1), p50 = quantile(sim, 0.5), p90 = quantile(sim, 0.9),
    ipred50 = median(Cc),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Observed medians read from Figure 2 by the maintainers.
fig2_median <- data.frame(
  occasion = c(rep("Occasion 1: time after infusion start (h)", 7),
               rep("Occasion 2: time after infusion end (h)", 5)),
  tplot = c(1, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 0, 1, 2, 4, 6),
  obs50 = c(0.40, 0.60, 0.75, 0.85, 0.80, 0.75, 0.75, 0.22, 0.12, 0.08, 0.055, 0.045)
)

ggplot(vpc, aes(tplot)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p10, ymax = p90), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50), colour = "steelblue", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(data = fig2_median, aes(tplot, obs50), shape = 1, size = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(~occasion, scales = "free_x") +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = "Dexmedetomidine (ng/mL)",
    caption = paste(
      "Simulated median and 10th-90th percentiles (with residual error) at a",
      "constant 0.8 ug/kg/h; circles: observed medians read from Figure 2."
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw()

occ1_cmp <- vpc |>
  dplyr::filter(grepl("Occasion 1", occasion)) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(fig2_median, by = c("occasion", "tplot")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (p50 - obs50) / obs50) |>
  dplyr::select(tplot, obs50, p50, pct_diff)
occ1_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Time after start (h)" = tplot,
    "Figure 2 observed median (ng/mL)" = obs50,
    "Simulated median (ng/mL)" = p50,
    "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Occasion 1: simulated median at 0.8 ug/kg/h vs the observed median of Figure 2.")
```

During the first 24 h the simulated median at the constant starting rate
has the shape of the observed median of Figure 2 and lies about 20% above it
(11-42% at the individual times). The children's rates were titrated from the
first hours on, and the observed end-of-infusion median (about 0.2 ng/mL) is
far below the simulation because rates had been stepped down before stopping,
so the absolute level is not a calibrated comparison. The shape of the
post-infusion decline is compared below on a scale normalised to the
end-of-infusion value.

```{r decline}
decline <- sim_c |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= t_end - 0.01) |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::mutate(rel = Cc / Cc[which.min(time)], tafter = pmax(time - t_end, 0)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::filter(tafter %in% c(1, 2, 4, 6)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(tafter) |>
  dplyr::summarise(model_rel = median(rel), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    fig2_median |>
      dplyr::filter(grepl("Occasion 2", occasion)) |>
      dplyr::mutate(paper_rel = obs50 / 0.22) |>
      dplyr::select(tafter = tplot, paper_rel),
    by = "tafter"
  )
decline |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Time after end (h)" = tafter,
    "Model median C/C_end" = model_rel,
    "Figure 2 median ratio" = paper_rel
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Post-infusion decline relative to the end-of-infusion concentration.")

early <- decline |> dplyr::filter(tafter %in% c(1, 2))
stopifnot(
  # Occasion 1: same level as the observed median despite the unknown
  # titration; a mis-transcribed CL or V moves this by far more.
  abs(median(occ1_cmp$pct_diff)) < 40,
  # First 2 h after the infusion: the fast decline driven by the larger
  # occasion-2 central volume matches the observed medians.
  all(abs(early$model_rel / early$paper_rel - 1) < 0.25)
)
```

The simulated decline over the first two hours matches the observed medians.
Later, the observed medians flatten more than the simulation; the observed
ratio of medians also reflects which children were still sampled at 4-6 h
and their stepped-down rates, so this is a qualitative comparison only.

# PKNCA validation

Non-compartmental analysis of the cohort without residual error (`Cc`, IIV
retained): Cmax and AUC over the first 24 h (occasion 1) and the terminal
half-life over the 6 h after the infusion. The paper reports no NCA results,
so there is no published comparator; the table summarises the simulation.

```{r pknca}
grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 24, by = 1), t_end - 0.01, t_end + c(5, 10, 20) / 60, t_end + seq(0.5, 6, by = 0.5))))
ev_n <- cohort |>
  dplyr::rowwise() |>
  dplyr::reframe(
    id = id,
    time = c(0, grid),
    evid = c(1, rep(0, length(grid))),
    amt = c(0.8 * WT * t_end, rep(0, length(grid))),
    rate = c(0.8 * WT, rep(0, length(grid))),
    cmt = "central",
    WT = WT, PNA = PNA
  )
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20160603)
sim_n <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, ev_n) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = "0.8 ug/kg/h x 97 h")

conc_df <- sim_n |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
dose_df <- cohort |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0, amt = 0.8 * WT * t_end, treatment = "0.8 ug/kg/h x 97 h") |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | treatment + id, concu = "ng/mL", timeu = "h")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id, doseu = "ug")
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, t_end),
  end = c(24, t_end + 6),
  cmax = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  auclast = c(TRUE, FALSE),
  half.life = c(FALSE, TRUE)
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
summary(nca_res)

hl <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "half.life")
stopifnot(
  # Post-infusion terminal phase within the 6-h window: hours, not minutes
  # or days, for a drug with CL ~ 0.8 L/h/kg and Vss ~ 1.7 L/kg.
  median(hl$PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE) > 1,
  median(hl$PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE) < 10
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Posterior means as point estimates.** Table 3 and Table 2S report the
  posterior mean and 90% highest-density interval; the model uses the means.
  The fractional occasion changes `fP` are entered as `e_occ2_<param> = fP - 1`
  so that the occasion-2 value is `P * (1 + e_occ2_<param>)`, which is the
  ratio the paper reports.
- **Occasion switch follows the authors' code.** The text describes the two
  occasions as separate parameter sets. The deposited WinBUGS / Component
  Pascal code implements them as a smooth logistic switch in time,
  `1 / (1 + exp(t - 30))`, with a slope of 1/h and a midpoint of 30 h after the
  infusion started, applied to CL, Q, V1, V2 in the ODEs and to V1 in the
  observation. The model reproduces that switch, so time zero must be the start
  of the infusion. For infusions shorter than about 30 h the occasion-2
  parameters would never take effect; the studied infusions all lasted at
  least 45 h.
- **Amount-based ODEs.** Methods equations 1-2 are written in concentrations,
  but the code integrates amounts with time-varying micro-constants and
  divides by the time-varying V1 to give the concentration. The model follows
  the code, so when V1 increases across the switch the concentration falls
  while the amount is conserved.
- **Postmenstrual age.** The code computes postmenstrual age in weeks as
  `4 * age_months + 40` (term birth, 4 weeks per month); `model()` uses the
  same conversion from the canonical postnatal-age column `PNA` (months).
  Baseline weight and age were used in the fit.
- **Residual error.** The paper uses a Student-t distribution on the log
  scale with scale 0.275 and 1.75 degrees of freedom, encoded as
  `lnorm(expSd) + dt(nu)`. With fewer than 2 degrees of freedom the residual
  variance is infinite, so simulated observations (`sim`) have very heavy
  tails; summarise them with medians and percentiles, not means. `nu` is the
  paper's name for the degrees of freedom, so `checkModelConventions()` warns
  that it is not one of the canonical residual-error names.
- **Covariate screen.** Sex, dose, infusion duration and PRISM score were
  examined graphically against the random effects and not retained (Figures
  6S and 7S); sex is listed in `covariatesDataExcluded`.
- **Table 3 typo.** The 90% interval for TE50 is printed as 61.7-47.8 weeks,
  which does not contain the mean of 42.5 weeks; only the mean is used.
- **Prior precision for the occasion fractions.** The Results select
  sigma_fP = 0.2; the printed code uses a precision `tau` of 100
  (sigma = 0.1). This affects only the prior, not the posterior means used
  here.
- **Validation targets** are digitised from Figures 2 and 3; the paper
  reports no NCA results. Infusion-rate histories were not published, so the
  cohort simulation uses the starting rate throughout.
- **Errata.** No erratum or correction was found (PubMed Central and the
  publisher's page, checked 2026-11-24).
